Cc: Priya Rao <priya@procure-cloudmed.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — evaluation timeline and success criteria

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. CloudMed is interested in running a 4-week evaluation of Redwood’s hosted inference for our patient-notes summarization workload. Procurement will want a clear MAP (mutual action plan) and measurable acceptance tests before we sign anything.

High-level asks from our side:
- Performance targets: 95th perc latency < 220ms for 512-token requests
- Quality: ROUGE-L delta vs baseline < 1.5 points on provided eval set
- Data controls: confirm logs retention policy and audit access
- Cost estimate and rollback plan if we fail acceptance

Can your team put together a one-page acceptance checklist and decision gates? We’d like the MAP by end of week so procurement can slot it into our vendor review.

Thanks—Alex
Alex Chou
Director, ML Systems
CloudMed Solutions

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. I’ve drafted a MAP and an acceptance-test checklist (attached) that maps your success criteria to measurable tests and decision gates. Key points up front:

- Evaluation duration: 4 weeks (30 days of traffic after integration).
- Exit gates: automatic pass if all tech thresholds met by day 28; automatic escalation to exec review if any critical threshold fails on day 30.
- Acceptance tests include latency/throughput, quality on your holdout set, KV cache hit-rate targets, and an SLO for error rates.

I attached: MAP_CloudMed_v1.xlsx and Acceptance_Tests_Checklist.md. Please review and flag any modifications. Once you confirm the functional criteria, we’ll add a procurement-friendly SLA draft for signatures.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm or edit the checklist by EOD Thu (4/15).
2) We schedule an integration-blocker call (30m) with your infra on Mon 4/13.
3) Redwood will run a smoke test with a 1% sample within 48h of integration.

Looping in Marissa and Rishi for technical acceptance-test owners.

—Hannah

CloudMed wants the MAP and measurable acceptance tests by Thu. I’ve attached the draft (MAP_CloudMed_v1.xlsx) and the Acceptance_Tests_Checklist.md. Can each of you own the sections below and reply with concrete thresholds we can commit to? Keep answers short so I can paste into the doc.

Marissa — model quality and eval harness (what sample size, metric thresholds, null-hypothesis test?).
Rishi — runtime & infra (latency distributions, cache hit-rate, error-rate SLO).

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-13T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudMed MAP — need acceptance-test owners and thresholds

Hannah —

Draft answers for the checklist (short):
- Eval harness: use CloudMed-provided holdout set (n=2,000 documents). Run 3 bootstrap samples of 1,000 each.
- Quality metric: ROUGE-L delta threshold <= 1.2 points (two-sided t-test, p < 0.05 against baseline).
- Human spot-check: sample 100 summaries reviewed by CloudMed QA; pass rate >= 90%.
- Regression policy: any single bootstrap sample showing >1.5 delta triggers immediate remediation window; failure after remediation (7 days) moves to escalation.

I’ll include a short note in the checklist describing the evaluation script and reproducibility steps.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood

Date: 2026-04-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP & acceptance gates — CloudMed evaluation

Alex/Priya —

Thanks for the prompt reviews — attached is the updated MAP and a short SLA-draft with procurement language included (SLA-draft-CloudMed-2026.pdf). Highlights of the final plan:

1) Timeline- Integration window: Apr 20–22 (infra smoke tests Apr 21)- Evaluation run: Apr 23–May 22 (30 days of live traffic post-integration)- Final decision gate: May 25 (procurement & exec signoff if pass)

2) Acceptance gates (pass conditions):
- Latency: 95th perc < 220ms for 512 tokens across week-long rolling windows for at least 3 of 4 weeks- Quality: ROUGE-L delta <= 1.2 with bootstrap p < 0.05 AND human QA pass rate >= 90%- Reliability: error-rate < 0.5%  (5xx/total) and KV cache hit-rate >= 72%

3) Failure & rollback- If any critical gate fails at final decision, CloudMed may stop traffic; Redwood will provide data exports and an integration termination package within 48 hours. There is a remediation window of 7 days before final contract-level escalation.

4) Procurement milestone: We’ll finalize and sign the MAP+SLA by 2026-05-01 to enable PO issuance.

Owners are documented in the MAP file; next actions:
- Priya: confirm procurement timeline (accept/adjust milestone by 4/16)
- Alex: confirm MAP text + sign-off on acceptance gates by 4/16
- Redwood (Marissa/Rishi/Connor): prep smoke test plan and the reproducible eval script, deliverables due 4/20.

I’ll put the final files in the shared Drive and send a calendar invite for the integration call.

Best —
Hannah

Attachments: MAP_CloudMed_v1.xlsx, Acceptance_Tests_Checklist.md, SLA-draft-CloudMed-2026.pdf
